absent: Enabled energy model registration, cost, table, limit and capacity algorithms and their data layouts.
Physical storage and architecture hooks for the preemption counter and the scheduler entry behind checked enables.
Exact tracepoint, lockdep and barrier implementations behind state-change and preemption helpers.
Pressure aggregation periods, averaging math, trigger wakeup paths and realtime polling lifecycle.
Full task structure layout, job-control flag values and priority-lock protocol beyond state stores.
Command-name termination rules and sleep-timeout handling in blocking paths.

findings.text: When the energy model is compiled out this lane still exposes the full management surface for devices, cpus and domains, covering registration, lookup, energy estimation, table handling, cost computation, limit and binning updates, plus capacity and domain rebuild hooks. The presence of these names preserves link compatibility so scheduler and driver callers need no conditional compilation.

The compiled-out behavior is fail-safe and neutral. Creation-like requests report an invalid-argument failure, handle-returning queries yield null, numeric queries yield zero, and release or refresh operations have no effect. Callers therefore observe absence as an error or empty result rather than partial state.

The preemption counter packs several fields from the least significant bit upward, with eight bits each for preemption, soft interrupt and interrupt-disable state, then four bits for hard interrupt and a build-dependent width for non-maskable state. Each field has a shift, a mask covering its width, a single-unit offset, and a derived double soft offset used when interrupts are disabled.

A boot context begins with one preemption unit while a forked context begins with two disable units above the enabled base. The disable increment equals one unit in fully preemptible builds and zero otherwise, the lock increment follows the same choice, and the combined soft-plus-preempt lock step adds the double soft offset to the lock increment.

Interrupt nesting is inferred from masked counter portions, with soft state taken either from the current task record or from the counter depending on build. Separate predicates report non-maskable activity, hard activity, soft service, any soft or interrupt activity, task context, and atomic regions, while a level helper folds the combination into depths zero to three.

In preemptible configurations disabling preemption raises the counter and enabling lowers it under ordering barriers, with counting primitives for adding, subtracting and single-step changes. Checked enable paths test for a pending reschedule after decrementing and transfer to the scheduler only when one is pending, while unchecked paths simply decrement.

Tracing-exempt forms use raw counter adjustments with the same pairing discipline but without trace hooks. Nested helpers change the counter only in realtime builds and otherwise assert disabled state or do nothing. A non-preemptible build collapses every disable, enable and reschedule-check operation to a barrier and reports never preemptible.
The need-reschedule indication can be raised unconditionally or folded from thread flags so that a separately recorded request becomes visible to the next preemption check without loss.

Scheduler entry and exit notification relies on a table with separate arrival and departure callbacks and a notifier object that joins list linkage with a pointer to that table. Initialization prepares an empty linkage and attaches the caller-supplied table for later registration.

Available call sites include interrupt depth computation, realtime-model detection, overall preemptibility detection through any of full, lazy or realtime selection, notifier initialization, and nested disable and enable wrappers that internally select between counting and assertion.

Task accounting uses four categories for input wait, memory stall, running and combined memory-stall-running, with single-bit flags per category and an extra on-cpu bit. Resources enumerate input, memory, cpu and optionally interrupt, while pressure states enumerate some and full per resource plus a non-idle marker, with further bits for on-cpu pressure and reschedule signaling beyond the state range.

Per-cpu pressure data separates scheduler-written tallies, derived masks, time buckets and change timestamps from aggregator-written prior snapshots by cache alignment. Monitoring uses a window of duration, start, baseline and prior growth, a trigger joining selector, threshold, linkage, group link, wait queue, file handle, event state, window, rate-limit time, deferred flag and aggregator choice, and a group joining hierarchy, enable state, locks, per-cpu store, averages, work items, trigger sets and realtime polling controls with totals and deadlines.
When pressure support is unavailable the group object carries no members and the resource count is defined as zero, so no per-cpu or averaging storage is expected.

Disabled pressure stubs make initialization, memory-stall bracketing, cgroup release and restart inert while cgroup allocation reports success. Group selection returns the global object for the root identity and the per-cgroup object otherwise, and task migration publishes the new group-set reference without extra pressure accounting.

Task condition codes assign running to zero and distinct low bits to interruptible sleep, uninterruptible sleep, stopped, traced, exit dead, exit zombie, parked, dead, wake-kill, waking, no-load, new, realtime-lock wait, freezable, unsafe freezable, frozen and a maximum bound, with an any mask covering all lower bits. Combined values express killable sleep, stopped and traced flavors, idle, normal sleep, unsafe freezable and the report subset used for status display.

Running status is determined by an exact match on the volatile state field, while traced and stopped conditions are read from volatile job-control flags. A special-state grouping collects stopped, traced, parked, dead, waking and frozen values to validate that debug-tracked transitions use the appropriate setter.

Normal state changes combine debug validation and conditional tracing with an ordered store, using a barriered store for the synchronizing variant and a plain volatile store otherwise. Special transitions and realtime-lock save and restore additionally serialize on the task priority lock with interrupts controlled, require interrupts off for the realtime path, preserve the prior value across the wait, and clear the saved slot to running on restore. Current state is always retrieved through a single volatile read.
Task command storage accommodates sixteen bytes, and the maximum schedule timeout is the largest representable signed long, allowing effectively unbounded sleep.
Each public header defines a single inclusion guard macro on first inclusion so repeated inclusion within one translation unit contributes no further definitions.

Debug builds emit a one-time warning when a normal setter receives a special value or a special setter receives a normal value, and record the caller address for diagnosis. State-change tracing occurs only when its tracepoint is enabled, so production builds without debugging observe no checks or records.

Energy fallback handles may be null and numeric results zero, requiring explicit absence checks before dereference or use in scheduling and thermal decisions. Atomic context is defined as any nonzero nesting count, with a separate preempt-off test that excludes the baseline disable offset, so helpers must not assume zero means task context without also considering interrupt masks.
